tagline: Back roads through Lord Fairfax's country, and one on the ridge.
intro: Clarke County's byways are a tangle of back roads around Millwood, Boyce and White Post, with Howellsville Road following the Shenandoah River and Blue Ridge Mountain Road running along the top of the ridge itself.

This was Lord Fairfax's country. The only titled British proprietor to live in the American colonies kept his seat at Greenway Court, south of White Post, at the center of more than five million acres, and hired a young George Washington to survey them. Up on the ridge, the old weather station at Mount Weather served as Calvin Coolidge's summer White House in 1928. The government has since dug in underneath it.

moments.title: Burwell-Morgan Mill
moments.text: Daniel Morgan built this mill at Millwood about 1785 with Nathaniel Burwell's money, though a stone in the wall carved with the overseer's initials says 1782.

moments.title: White Post
moments.text: The crossroads is named for its white post, and the bronze plaque on it says Washington set the original to guide travelers to Lord Fairfax's house.

moments.title: Blue Ridge Mountain Road
moments.text: SR 601 keeps to the top of the Blue Ridge from Snickers Gap to Ashby Gap, and it is the road up to the Mount Weather emergency operations center.
